title: Chapter 118: He's Crazy
html:
“What are you talking about?” Chen Ge’s words only confused Doctor Gao further. He could no longer follow the man’s reasoning, though that was hardly his fault. Only Chen Ge knew about the black phone’s most important clue: the mission’s name, A Room of Three.

Unwilling to reveal the black phone, Chen Ge offered no explanation and left the room alone.

Men Nan experienced the same dream again and again, yet what he remembered most clearly was washing his hair. At first, the dream had not frightened him at all. Fear came only when the man began drawing closer. The true threat, then, was the man.

Men Nan’s account supported that conclusion. He felt no danger while washing his hair, but hostility overwhelmed him whenever the man approached. In the latest dream, the figure had reached his side and wrapped its hands around his throat. It clearly meant him harm.

Thus, among the three occupants of the room, Men Nan was the victim; of the other two, one wished to protect him and one to hurt him. In traditional Chinese belief, dreaming of washing one’s hair signified cleansing away misfortune. Perhaps the dream was warning Men Nan that danger was closing in.

After learning about Men Nan’s childhood, Chen Ge suspected his mother was the one protecting him. Mother and son had depended on each other, so she had no reason to cause him harm. The hostile figure, on the other hand, was probably Room 303’s former tenant.

When Chen Ge first entered Hai Ming Apartments, the strangely knotted red strings along the railings had caught his attention. They were part of a traditional method for warding off evil, and their presence suggested something malicious haunted the building.

The warning from the resident of Room 301 and the black phone’s mission hint only strengthened his suspicion.

If I want to identify the man in Men Nan’s dream and solve this problem, I have to enter Room 303. The black phone’s mission points there too.

Anything capable of attacking people through their dreams was no benevolent spirit. The presence in Room 303 was probably similar to the mirror monster he had faced before.

Time to face another monster.

The dead, like the living, could be good or evil. Chen Ge had no qualms about destroying those that preyed on others.

The man in Room 301 said someone died in 303 and that the room has remained vacant ever since. Whatever lingers there is probably the dead tenant’s malicious specter.Chen Ge had encountered several kinds of ghosts: lingering spirits were little more than scraps of consciousness; entities like Xiaoxiao were stronger; and the mirror monster stood above them. He estimated that Room 303’s occupant was comparable to the mirror monster.

I wasn’t afraid then, so why be afraid now? Besides, there are plenty of living people nearby if I need help.After asking Men Nan where to find the landlady, Chen Ge left Room 304 and knocked on Room 101 downstairs.

After a while, a heavyset woman in her fifties opened the door. She looked him up and down. “You want to rent a room?”

“Yes, my friend is living in Room 304, so I want to rent the room next to him: Room 303.”

“303 isn’t available. Choose another.”

“The room is empty; why isn’t it for rent?” Chen Ge asked.

“There are empty rooms on the fourth floor. If you refuse to take those, then leave.” The woman then closed the door, effectively ending the conversation.

Is she always that unfriendly, or did I strike a nerve? Either way, Room 303 is hiding something.Since the landlady clearly would not discuss the death there, Chen Ge changed tactics and returned to the third floor to knock on Room 301.

The television volume lowered, and the man that stank of alcohol came to answer the door. “You again?”

“Boss, could I have a moment of your time?” Chen Ge handed him a hundred-yuan note. The man pocketed it, and his expression immediately softened. “What do you want?”

“I want to know about the things that happened in Room 303. The more detailed, the better.”

“Room 303?” Rather than step outside, the middle-aged man waved Chen Ge in. Trash filled the cramped apartment, leaving barely enough room to stand.

After closing the door, the man raised the television’s volume. “You’re a curious one, aren’t you? Listen—for your sake and your friend’s, move out as soon as you can. This building isn’t a place just anyone can live.”

“What do you mean? Are the tenants chosen by some special criteria?”

“Funny you should ask—it has everything to do with Room 303.” The man grabbed a bottle from the table and swallowed a mouthful of beer. “Do you know the name of that room’s original tenant?”

“How would I know something like that?” Chen Ge tried his best to ignore the alcoholic breath that drifted out of the man’s mouth. It was difficult to tell whether the man was serious or merely making up a story.

“His name was Wang Haiming. This building belonged to him.”

“But I saw the landlady earlier. She appeared to be a woman in her fifties.”

“That’s his ex-wife.” The man glared at Chen Ge for interrupting. “Wang Haiming struck it rich, abandoned his wife, and married a woman no one knew anything about. A few years later, that woman took all his money and had him committed to a psychiatric hospital. In the end, his ex-wife took pity on him, secured his release, and gave him a place to stay—Room 303.”

“Wang Haiming was once in a mental hospital?” Chen Ge was reminded of the black phone’s mission hint—He came from the Third Sick Hall.

“Yes. Whether or not he was insane when he went in, he certainly wasn’t normal when he came out.”

“Abnormal? What do you mean?”

“Here’s one example.” The man tapped his temple. “Every night at midnight, Wang Haiming would smash his head against the wall, as if something had burrowed into his brain and he wanted to crack his skull open to get it out. He screamed, wailed, and argued with himself. Sometimes he kept going even after blood covered his face. No one could restrain him; more than once, we had to call the police.”
